title: The Complete Guide to Customer Reactivation for Service Businesses | Winback Engine Blog

facts.fact: Industry data shows that 60–70% of a typical service business's customer base is lapsed at any given time.
facts.quote: Industry data shows that 60–70% of a typical service business’s customer base is lapsed at any given time.

facts.fact: Reactivation campaigns typically cost 5–10x less per converted customer than new acquisition, according to the vendor's guide.
facts.quote: reactivation campaigns typically cost 5–10x less per converted customer than new acquisition.

facts.fact: Cost per contact for new customer acquisition is $50–$200, while cost per contact for customer reactivation is $5–$20, per the vendor's comparison table.
facts.quote: | Cost per contact | $50–$200 | $5–$20 |

facts.fact: Conversion rate for new customer acquisition is 1–3%, versus 15–40% for customer reactivation, per the vendor's comparison table.
facts.quote: | Conversion rate | 1–3% | 15–40% |

facts.fact: Time to first booking is 2–8 weeks for new customer acquisition versus 3–14 days for customer reactivation, per the vendor's table.
facts.quote: | Time to first booking | 2–8 weeks | 3–14 days |

facts.fact: A lapsed customer who rebooks has a 60–70% probability of becoming active again long-term, compared with a 20–30% retention rate for newly acquired customers, per the vendor.
facts.quote: A lapsed customer who rebooks has a 60–70% probability of becoming active again long-term, compared to a 20–30% retention rate for newly acquired customers.

facts.fact: In service businesses, a lapsed customer is typically someone who hasn't booked in 90–180 days, depending on service cadence.
facts.quote: a “lapsed” customer is typically someone who hasn’t booked in 90–180 days (the exact threshold depends on your service cadence).

facts.fact: The guide suggests setting the lapsed threshold at roughly 1.5–2x the typical repeat-visit interval for each service.
facts.quote: set the lapsed threshold at roughly 1.5–2x that interval.

facts.fact: Gym/fitness studios with 2–4 visits per week are treated as lapsed after 30–60 days of inactivity, per the vendor's table.
facts.quote: | Gym/fitness studio | 2–4x per week | 30–60 days inactive |

facts.fact: Dental practices with about 2 visits per year are treated as lapsed after 7+ months since last visit, per the vendor's table.
facts.quote: | Dental practice | 2x per year | 7+ months since last visit |

facts.fact: Med spas with visits every 4–8 weeks are treated as lapsed after 90+ days inactive, per the vendor's table.
facts.quote: | Med spa | Every 4–8 weeks | 90+ days inactive |

facts.fact: Hair salons with visits every 4–6 weeks are treated as lapsed after 90+ days inactive, per the vendor's table.
facts.quote: | Hair salon | Every 4–6 weeks | 90+ days inactive |

facts.fact: Pet grooming with visits every 6–8 weeks is treated as lapsed after 120+ days inactive, per the vendor's table.
facts.quote: | Pet grooming | Every 6–8 weeks | 120+ days inactive |

facts.fact: Calling every lapsed customer yields a 15–20% reactivation rate at $45–70 per reactivated customer, per the vendor's table.
facts.quote: | Call every lapsed customer | 15–20% | $45–70 |

facts.fact: Calling a scored, segmented list yields a 30–40% reactivation rate at $18–30 per reactivated customer, per the vendor's table.
facts.quote: | Call a scored, segmented list | 30–40% | $18–30 |

facts.fact: Emailing every lapsed customer yields a 2–4% reactivation rate at $8–15 per reactivated customer, per the vendor's table.
facts.quote: | Email every lapsed customer | 2–4% | $8–15 |

facts.fact: In the vendor's 5-factor reactivation score, Recency carries a 30% weight, Frequency 25%, Value 20%, Tenure 15%, and Engagement 10%.
facts.quote: | **Recency** | 30% | How recently they lapsed | Last visit date |

facts.fact: Under the vendor's recency scoring band, customers lapsed 12+ months receive 3 of 30 recency points.
facts.quote: 12+ months = 3.

facts.fact: Under the page's lead-scoring model, a customer with 2+ years of tenure earns 15 points, the maximum for the tenure category.
facts.quote: **Tenure (15 max):** customer 2+ years = 15; 1–2 years = 12; 6–12 months = 8; under 6 months = 4.

facts.fact: Under the page's engagement scoring, opening an email in the last 30 days earns 5 points, the maximum engagement points for that action.
facts.quote: **Engagement (10 max):** opened an email in last 30 days = 5; visited the website in last 30 days = 3; follows on social = 2.

facts.fact: Tier A (Hot, score 70–100) calls for a phone call within 48 hours, with an expected reactivation rate of 35–50%.
facts.quote: | **A — Hot** | 70–100 | Phone call first, within 48 hours | 35–50% |

facts.fact: Tier B (Warm, score 45–69) has an expected reactivation rate of 20–35%.
facts.quote: | **B — Warm** | 45–69 | Phone call, second batch | 20–35% |

facts.fact: Tier C (Cool, score 25–44) has an expected reactivation rate of 10–20%.
facts.quote: | **C — Cool** | 25–44 | Email + SMS sequence; phone if budget allows | 10–20% |

facts.fact: Tier D (Cold, score 0–24) has an expected reactivation rate of 3–8%.
facts.quote: | **D — Cold** | 0–24 | Email only, or exclude | 3–8% |

facts.fact: The page states that Tier A and B customers convert at 3–5 times the rate of lower tiers.
facts.quote: These customers convert at 3–5x the rate of the lower tiers and generate more revenue when they return.

facts.fact: The page describes the 'golden window' as customers lapsed 1–3 times their normal visit cycle.
facts.quote: The **golden window** is customers lapsed 1–3x their normal visit cycle

facts.quote: Anyone who received a win-back campaign in the last 90 days (avoid fatigue)
